key_insight: Glioblastoma necrosis may be an active, mutation-driven process in which tumor-associated neutrophil extracellular traps and HMGB2 amplify tumor-cell necroptosis.
clinical_relevance: MRI-measured necrotic volume and high HMGB2 expression may help identify high-risk glioblastoma, while the associated inflammatory cascade offers investigational therapeutic targets.
method: Integrated clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets.
Mapped tumor niches using single-cell spatial transcriptomics.
Investigated mechanisms with protein immunofluorescence in a TP53/PTEN/NF1 co-mutant mouse model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports public genomic datasets totaling n=3,639, associations between MRI necrotic volume and poorer survival, and multi-cohort validation of a high-risk HMGB2-high signature.
watch_item: Mechanistic and treatment findings remain preclinical; the abstract does not establish prospective biomarker performance or therapeutic benefit in patients.
paper_title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
